memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD
drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land. The
waters were divided, and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with
a wall of water on their right and on their left." - Ex 14:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sea opens. And notice how God does it: with a strong east wind, all night
long.

There is something worth seeing in that detail. God used a wind. He worked
through means, through something ordinary, though the result was utterly beyond
nature. It took all night, which means Israel spent hours in the dark listening
to wind and water while the enemy waited behind the cloud.

Then, dry ground. Not mud. Not a difficult wade. Dry.

God does not do half rescues. When He makes a way, it is a way you can actually
walk on. He thought about the elderly, the children, the livestock, the
possessions.

Hebrews 11:29 records this as an act of faith: "By faith the people passed
through the Red Sea as on dry land." Somebody had to step in first, between
those walls of water, trusting they would hold.

We should say plainly that God does not promise to part every sea in front of
us. Sometimes He brings His people through the water rather than around it. But
Isaiah 43:2 holds the promise steady: "When you pass through the waters, I will
be with you."

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you need God to make a way that does not currently exist?
2. Can you trust Him to be with you even if the sea does not part?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You make ways where there is no way. Whether You part the water or walk
me through it, be with me. Amen.
